concepts.definition: An orderly data format made of key-value pairs, with double quotation marks and items separated by commas.
concepts.pitfall: Using single quotation marks or leaving a comma after the last item; both produce invalid JSON.

concepts.definition: Asking the model for an answer in an orderly format a program can read, instead of free sentences.
concepts.example: Getting the sentiment and topic extracted from a comment as JSON.
concepts.pitfall: Never stating the format; the model may choose a different format each time.

concepts.definition: Using the same key names in the instructions, in the example and in the validation code.
concepts.example: Writing "duygu" and "konu" in all of them.
concepts.pitfall: Writing "duygu" (sentiment) in the instructions and "his" (feeling) in the example; the model cannot know which one to choose.

concepts.definition: Checking that the output that arrives is valid JSON and carries the expected keys.
concepts.example: Parsing it with JSON.parse, then checking whether "duygu" and "konu" are there.
concepts.pitfall: Skipping validation and assuming the output will always arrive in proper form.

concepts.definition: Sending the request again, or giving an error, when validation fails.
concepts.example: If it is invalid in all three attempts, telling the user "I can't answer right now".
concepts.pitfall: Retrying forever; you need to put a limit on the number of attempts.

concepts.definition: Telling the prompt "write nothing except JSON".
concepts.example: A constraint written to reduce opening sentences such as "Here is the result:".
concepts.pitfall: Treating the constraint as a guarantee; the model may still add an explanation.

quiz.prompt: When asked for JSON, the model mostly gives a proper answer. Why do you still need to validate the output?
options: Because JSON can carry only one key
Because JSON.parse never gives an error
Because validation makes the model smarter
Because the model can sometimes produce invalid JSON or a missing key, and it cannot guarantee this will not happen
quiz.explanation: The model writes using probability; it is usually proper but there is no guarantee. It may add an explanation in front, miss a quotation mark or forget a key. Validation does not change the model; it only catches the error. JSON.parse throws an error on invalid text.

quiz.prompt:
The model gave this answer. What happens when this code runs?

```
const yanit = 'Here is the result: {"duygu": "olumlu"}'
const veri = JSON.parse(yanit)
console.log(veri.duygu)
```
options: JSON.parse throws an error, nothing is printed
Here is the result: olumlu is printed
quiz.explanation: The text is not valid JSON: it starts with "Here is the result:", and the JSON must be the whole text. In this case JSON.parse throws a SyntaxError; the console.log line is never reached. That is why the "give only JSON" constraint and validation are used together.

quiz.prompt:
The output below, produced by a model, cannot be parsed with JSON.parse. What is the problem?

```
{"duygu": "olumlu", "konu": "robot dersi",}
```
options: There is an extra comma after the last item
The values are written in double quotation marks
quiz.explanation: JSON does not allow a comma after the last item. Keys with Turkish letters and values in double quotation marks are valid; having two keys is not a problem either. The fix: delete the comma at the end.

quiz.prompt: An app got 50 replies from the model, and 3 of them could not be parsed with JSON.parse. What percentage of the replies are valid JSON?
quiz.explanation: There are 50 − 3 = 47 valid replies. 47 / 50 × 100 = 94. An error rate of 6 per cent may look small; but the app still has to deal with it by retrying or giving an error.

quiz.prompt: The reply is valid JSON, but the "konu" (topic) key you expected is missing. What should the app do?
options: Notice that "konu" is missing and retry or give an error
Use the data as it is, because JSON.parse succeeded
Look at the Prompt checker's score
quiz.explanation: Validation has two layers: is it valid JSON, and are the expected keys there. If a key is missing, retry or give an error. Silently deleting it hides the error. The checker in the Workshop judges only the prompt; it does not validate the model's reply.
